Mark Teixeira

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 21, Bexar County, Texas · Open seat

Former Major League Baseball player; investor in small businesses, startups and real estate

Mark Teixeira is a former Major League Baseball first baseman who played for the Texas Rangers, Atlanta Braves, Los Angeles Angels and New York Yankees, and later worked as an ESPN analyst and investor. He won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for Texas' 21st Congressional District outright with 60.9% of the vote against 11 other candidates, for the open seat held by U.S. Rep. Chip Roy. He faces Democrat Kristin Hook in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Teixeira stands

Immigration and border security
Supports stronger border enforcement and deportations.
Federal spending and deficit
Proposes expanding DOGE to cut what he calls wasteful federal spending, and calls for more auditing and oversight of public spending. Wants to reduce the deficit through spending cuts rather than raising tax rates.
Taxes
Opposes raising tax rates to address the deficit and supports spending cuts instead, according to the Austin American-Statesman editorial board's account of his position.
Energy
Proposes expanding Texas oil, gas and nuclear production to restore U.S. 'energy dominance' and lower costs for families. Supports federal support for grid modernization, research and infrastructure.
Health care
Says he wants to lower health care costs, expand consumer choice and reduce Washington's control over health care decisions. Proposes targeting fraud, waste and abuse in Medicare and Medicaid, limiting program care to eligible citizens, and opening insurance markets to more competition.
Abortion
Says elective abortion should be allowed only when the mother's life is threatened. Opposes taxpayer funding for abortion providers, including Planned Parenthood, and supports enforcing the Comstock Act's ban on shipping abortion-inducing drugs across state lines.
Education
Supports school choice and empowering parents in education. Supports eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and returning control to states and communities.
Gun rights
His platform supports gun rights.
Term limits
Supports congressional term limits.
Marriage and gender issues
Says marriage is a union of one man and one woman. Agrees with the statement that physically or socially transitioning a child to the opposite sex is child abuse.

Background

  • Republican nominee, U.S. House, Texas District 21 (won March 3, 2026 primary with 60.9%)
  • Has not held elected office
  • ESPN baseball analyst, 2017–2020
  • Investor in small businesses, startups and real estate since retiring from baseball
  • Has worked with the Texas Public Policy Foundation; advocate for school choice
  • Education: business administration degree, Georgia Tech
  • Endorsed by President Donald Trump and Gov. Greg Abbott
